nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-02.title: Divisibility by 7
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-02.body:
$6356=7\cdot908$ and $7q$ are multiples of $7$, so $p$ is a multiple of $7$; being prime, $p=7$. Then $7q=6349$, so $q=907$, which is prime (it has no prime factor up to $\sqrt{907}<31$). So $q=907$ is the only value.

**Answer: 907**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-05.title: Right triangle
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-05.body:
Let $O$ be the center. $OA\perp BC$, $OA=6$, $OB=8$, so $AB=\sqrt{64-36}=2\sqrt7$. The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord, so $BC=4\sqrt7$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt7$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-05.title: Power of a point
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-05.body:
$A$ is the midpoint of chord $BC$. The power of $A$ with respect to the large circle is $AB\cdot AC=8^2-6^2=28$, and $AB=AC$, so $AB=\sqrt{28}=2\sqrt7$ and $BC=4\sqrt7$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt7$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-06.title: Count vertices and edges
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-06.body:
The faces have $3\cdot20=60$ corners and each vertex is counted $5$ times, so there are $12$ vertices. Each edge lies on $2$ faces, so there are $\frac{3\cdot20}{2}=30$ edges. The $\binom{12}{2}=66$ segments joining vertices include the $30$ edges, leaving $36$ diagonals.

**Answer: 36**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-06.title: Count from one vertex
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-06.body:
Each of the $12$ vertices is joined by edges to $5$ others, so it is joined by diagonals to $12-1-5=6$ others. Each diagonal has two ends, so there are $\frac{12\cdot6}{2}=36$ diagonals.

**Answer: 36**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-07.title: Pythagorean theorem twice
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-07.body:
$AC$ is a face diagonal, $AC=\sqrt2$. The edge $CG$ is perpendicular to the face, so triangle $ACM$ has a right angle at $C$ with $CM=\frac12$. Then $AM=\sqrt{2+\frac14}=\frac32$.

**Answer: $\frac32$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-08.title: Recognize a fifth power
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-08.body:
Expanding and collecting gives $x^5-5x^4+10x^3-10x^2+5x+10=0$. The first five terms match $(x-1)^5=x^5-5x^4+10x^3-10x^2+5x-1$, so the equation is $(x-1)^5+11=0$, i.e. $(x-1)^5=-11$. Its real root is $x=1-\sqrt[5]{11}$, so $(a,b)=(1,11)$.

**Answer: $(1, 11)$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-09.title: Square and compare
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-09.body:
$(a+bi)^2=(a^2-b^2)+2abi=48+14i$, so $a^2-b^2=48$ and $ab=7$. Positive integers with product $7$ are $\{1,7\}$, and $a^2-b^2=48>0$ forces $a=7$, $b=1$. Check: $(7+i)^2=49-1+14i$.

**Answer: $(7, 1)$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-10.title: Count exponent choices
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-10.body:
The coefficient counts solutions of $i+5j+10k=13$ with $i,j,k\ge0$ (exponents $i$, $5j$, $10k$ from the three factors). If $k=1$: $i+5j=3$, so $j=0$: one way. If $k=0$: $i+5j=13$ with $j=0,1,2$: three ways. Total $4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-10.title: Multiply truncated factors
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-10.body:
Only terms up to $x^{13}$ matter. $(1+x^5+x^{10})(1+x^{10})=1+x^5+2x^{10}+\cdots$. Multiplying by $1+x+\cdots+x^{13}$, the $x^{13}$ term comes from $x^{13}\cdot1+x^8\cdot x^5+x^3\cdot2x^{10}$, coefficient $1+1+2=4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-11.title: Similar triangles
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-11.body:
$12^2+16^2=20^2$, so $\angle C=90^\circ$. Triangles $ADE$ and $ACB$ share angle $A$ and have right angles at $D$ and $C$, so they are similar: $\frac{DE}{AD}=\frac{CB}{AC}=\frac{12}{16}$. With $AD=10$, $DE=\frac{15}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{15}{2}$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-11.title: Tangent of angle A
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-11.body:
In right triangle $ABC$, $\tan A=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac34$. In right triangle $ADE$, $DE=AD\tan A=10\cdot\frac34=\frac{15}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{15}{2}$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-12.title: Prime exponents
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-12.body:
We need positive integers with $x^2=\frac72y^3$, i.e. $2x^2=7y^3$. Compare prime exponents on both sides:
- For $2$: the exponent in $2x^2$ is odd, and in $7y^3$ it is a multiple of $3$, so it is an odd multiple of $3$; at least $3$.
- For $7$: the exponent in $2x^2$ is even, and in $7y^3$ it is one more than a multiple of $3$; the smallest such is $4$.
- Any other prime appears to an exponent divisible by both $2$ and $3$; the smallest choice is $0$.

So the minimum is $2x^2=2^3\cdot7^4$, giving $x^2=2^2\cdot7^4=9604$. Check: $9604=98^2$ and $\frac72\cdot14^3=\frac72\cdot2744=9604$.

**Answer: 9604**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-12.title: Search over cubes
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-12.body:
$\frac72y^3$ must be an integer square, so $y$ is even and $7\mid y$ (since $7y^3$ needs an even power of $7$, $y$ must contain $7$). So $y$ is a multiple of $14$; $y=14$ gives $\frac72\cdot2744=9604=98^2$, a square. Any smaller $y$ is not a multiple of $14$, so $9604$ is the smallest.

**Answer: 9604**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-13.title: Remove two numbers
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-13.body:
The product of all eight numbers is $8!=40320=10\cdot4032$. So the two numbers left out have product $10$; the only such pair in the set is $2$ and $5$. The six numbers are $1,3,4,6,7,8$.

**Answer: $1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-14.title: Cube both sides
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-14.body:
Cubing, $354+147\sqrt[3]{11}+21\sqrt[3]{121}=a^3+b+3a^2\sqrt[3]{b}+3a\sqrt[3]{b^2}$. Matching $\sqrt[3]{b}=\sqrt[3]{11}$ (so $\sqrt[3]{b^2}=\sqrt[3]{121}$) suggests $b=11$, $3a^2=147$, $3a=21$, i.e. $a=7$; and indeed $a^3+b=343+11=354$. Since a real number has exactly one real cube root and $7+\sqrt[3]{11}$ cubes to the given expression, $(a,b)=(7,11)$.

**Answer: $(7, 11)$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-15.title: Reduce mod 360
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-15.body:
We need $10^{100}\bmod 360$. Since $360=8\cdot9\cdot5$: $10^{100}\equiv0\pmod 8$ and $\pmod 5$, and $10^{100}\equiv1\pmod 9$. The residue $r<360$ is a multiple of $40$ that is $1\bmod 9$: $r=280$. So $\sin(10^{100})^\circ=\sin280^\circ=-\sin80^\circ$, and we need $\sin n^\circ=\sin80^\circ$. The smallest positive solution is $n=80$ (the solutions are $n\equiv80$ or $100\pmod{360}$).

**Answer: 80**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-16.title: Stars and bars
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-16.body:
A combination is determined by how many times each of the $6$ letters N, Y, C, I, M, L appears: nonnegative integers $a+b+c+d+e+f=6$. By stars and bars (6 stars, 5 bars) there are $\binom{11}{5}=462$.

**Answer: 462**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-17.title: Three consecutive integers
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-17.body:
$n^3-n=(n-1)n(n+1)$. If $n$ is odd, $n-1$ and $n+1$ are both even, so $4$ divides the product. If $4\mid n$, it divides too. If $n\equiv2\pmod4$, the neighbors are odd and $n$ has only one factor of $2$, so $4$ does not divide. There are $25$ such $n\le100$, leaving $100-25=75$.

**Answer: 75**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-18.title: Area ratios and similar triangles
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-18.body:
Let the sides be $a=6$, $b=8$, $c=12$ with altitudes $h_a,h_b,h_c$, and let $P$ be at distance $\alpha h_a$, $\beta h_b$, $\gamma h_c$ from the three sides. Then $\alpha=\frac{[PBC]}{[ABC]}$, and similarly for $\beta,\gamma$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1$.

The segment through $P$ parallel to side $a$ is at distance $(1-\alpha)h_a$ from the opposite vertex, so it cuts off a triangle similar to $ABC$ with ratio $1-\alpha$ and has length $6(1-\alpha)$. Likewise the other two have lengths $8(1-\beta)$ and $12(1-\gamma)$. Setting all equal to $L$:
$$1-\alpha=\frac L6,\quad 1-\beta=\frac L8,\quad 1-\gamma=\frac L{12}.$$
Adding, $3-1=L\left(\frac16+\frac18+\frac1{12}\right)=\frac{3L}{8}$, so $L=\frac{16}{3}$.

**Answer: $\frac{16}{3}$**

nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-18.title: Pieces of the sides
nyciml-2014-15-spring-junior-18.body:
The three segments cut off three small triangles at $P$, each similar to the original; let their ratios be $x$, $y$, $z$, where the triangle resting on the side of length $12$ has ratio $x$, the one on the side of length $6$ has ratio $y$, and the one on the side of length $8$ has ratio $z$. Using the parallelograms formed, each side of the big triangle is split into three pieces equal to the corresponding sides of the three small triangles, so $x+y+z=1$.

The segment parallel to the side of length $12$ consists of the corresponding sides of the two small triangles not resting on that side: $L=12y+12z$. Similarly $L=6x+6z$ and $L=8x+8y$. So $y+z=\frac L{12}$, $x+z=\frac L6$, $x+y=\frac L8$; adding, $2=L\cdot\frac38$ and $L=\frac{16}{3}$.

**Answer: $\frac{16}{3}$**
